the use of monotherapy, despite being still widespread in clinical practice, does not allow to reach the new BP treatment targets suggested from recent hypertension guidelines.

, despite monotherapy may be a useful and safe approach in the treatment of uncomplicated mild hypertension, it may not be sufficient to obtain the BP targets in the majority of hypertensive patients.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, despite the guidelines recommend a combination therapy to improve the BP control, monotherapy is widely used in the real clinical practice and, as a consequence, the achievement of the BP treatment goals is unsatisfactory.

, in the setting of clinical practice, monotherapy is widely used to treat hypertension, with a poor BP control, despite the availability of effective combination therapies, which are still underused.

monotherapy is a less effective treatment strategy to reach BP targets, compared to dual or triple combination, though it may represent an effective strategy to improve BP control in elderly hypertensive patients.

, despite combination therapy is the recommended approach to improve blood pressure control, monotherapy is often preferred in clinical practice, with poor BP control, especially if compared with combination therapies.
